scope: An additive codex-state SQLite commit/checkout primitive. No Current record, trust credential, Root parser or normal product caller is added by this batch.

meaningful_production_change.connection_creation: Each physical connection installs the real SQLx/SQLite commit hook before it can reach the caller, then awaits checkout coordination.
meaningful_production_change.connection_reuse: The existing idle-connection before_acquire callback also awaits checkout coordination; SQLx does not call before_acquire for new connections.
meaningful_production_change.commit_boundary: SQLite runs the supplied bounded synchronous Fn()->bool for explicit and implicit commits; false converts the real commit into rollback. Completion of checkout coordination never substitutes for this final callback.
meaningful_production_change.lock_order: connection.lock_handle() is held only while installing the hook; its lexical scope ends before awaiting before_checkout. Callback contracts prohibit re-entering this pool and prohibit retaining a lock required by the commit hook.
meaningful_production_change.initialization_limit: SQLx applies connection options before after_connect. The owner must retain its file/initialization fence while opening; this method does not make path reopen safe or protect setup before the hook.
meaningful_production_change.trusted_owner_limit: The owner must keep the raw pool private, keep the independently authenticated Current/writer gate alive, and must not replace the SQLite hook. This API alone cannot prevent an independent legacy connection from writing.

facts: The actual donor binder consumes the sole exclusive recovered CognitiveStore handle and refuses an already managed owner.
It manages the existing whole-pool gate, validates independently supplied Current against the exact recovery cut, rolls back its guard transaction, and closes the old pool.
Lines 78-88 call the coordinated writer API with connection_gate.commit_allowed and coordinator.before_checkout.
Lines 103-119 still require open_durable_observation_pool and open_durable_read_barrier, which this R2c does not add.
Actual checkout coordination serializes the protected receipt transition.
A failed transition fences writes; read-only inspection may still obtain a connection. That explains the Future<Output=()> contract without treating success of checkout as permission to commit.

sources.claim: The documented boolean is true to permit and false to veto; only one hook exists per SQLite connection.
SQLite converts a nonzero native hook response into rollback and prohibits reentrant SQL in the callback.
SQLx converts false (or a caught callback panic) to the native nonzero veto; set_commit_hook installs and retains the real callback.
before_acquire runs on idle reused connections and explicitly does not run for new connections.
Fresh and reused acquisitions follow distinct callbacks; a new connection is returned only after successful after_connect. Cancellation drops the in-progress owned connection.
DatabaseError.code reflects the actual extended SQLite error code, allowing exact SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_COMMITHOOK rejection rather than any generic failure.

primary_api_evidence.limit: The primary implementation was read at the upstream version tag resolved to its commit and byte-hashed. No local Cargo source extraction or compile was performed; the registry checksum remains the project's existing lock identity.

physical_controls.name: sqlite::commit_gate_tests::commit_gate_rejects_explicit_transaction_after_revocation
assertions: A real explicit transaction inserts while the gate is true; the gate is then revoked before COMMIT.
The actual COMMIT must return SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_COMMITHOOK, and a separate read-only SQLite pool must observe no row.
Restoring the same gate permits a subsequent write, and reopening the reader observes exactly that committed row.

physical_controls.name: sqlite::commit_gate_tests::commit_gate_covers_pool_growth_and_replacement
assertions: Five simultaneously held pool connections each reject actual implicit INSERT commits.
An explicitly closed connection is replaced while the other four remain held, and the replacement must reject its real INSERT too.
A later permitted write persists exactly one expected row through an independently opened reader.

physical_controls.name: sqlite::commit_gate_tests::checkout_callback_blocks_initial_connect_and_reused_connection
assertions: A real semaphore gate is entered during initial connection setup; the pool-opening future remains Pending before release.
Four held connections force the fifth acquisition to reuse the sole released connection; the callback must enter and remain Pending again.
A TEMP table marker proves the returned connection is physically the same reused SQLite connection.

physical_controls.name: sqlite::commit_gate_tests::cancelled_checkout_does_not_release_uncoordinated_connection
assertions: Cancel a real reused-connection acquisition only after observing that its coordination callback entered and the acquisition remained Pending.
The subsequent acquisition must have no original TEMP marker, proving the canceled connection was discarded.
The replacement must still reject an actual write with the exact commit-hook error, and a separate reader observes no row.

tests.test_budget: Only the four new tests use a 5-second bound for their own synchronization/checkout steps. No original test or production timeout, retry, filter, permission or assertion changes.
tests.cleanup: No test spawns its own detached task. Successful paths explicitly close every held connection and pool. Dropped in-progress SQLx acquisition futures retain SQLx's owned-connection cleanup; cancellation is tested by acquiring a fresh physical replacement. Fixture Drop performs best-effort removal of its unique private directory on an error; this is not a claim of synchronous descendant cleanup.
tests.baseline_claim: These are executable physical negative/positive controls of a new API. They are not a claimed reproduction against the old source, where this API does not exist.
tests.original_tests: Every pre-existing test file is unchanged. The original state test count must be taken from the actual selected native roster; it is not guessed.
tests.actual_linked_runtime_version: First existing new test queries sqlite_version() on the actual compiled pool before its real write/COMMIT. Native receipts must retain the observed version; upstream source is not itself runtime version evidence.
